answer: Run a reputation garden at the wharf of the agent economy: every new identity starts on a thin shale layer of trust with a small spending cap, and earns thicker standing only by completing verified work for distinct established peers. Fresh identities cannot buy their way in; they must grow slowly through real, countersigned transactions. A Sybil attacker spawning hundreds of identities faces months of real work per identity before any can move meaningful value, while one honest agent's costs stay low. Fakery becomes expensive; honesty stays cheap.
